title: Introduction
text: kadr takes screenshots and records the screen.

title: Install
text: Use a release build, or build kadr from source with Rust 1.95 or newer.

title: Capture
text: Everything that takes a picture of the screen: an area, a window, the whole screen or every screen, a long scrolling shot, a shot on a self-timer.

title: Editor
text: The editor is where a screenshot gets its arrows, boxes, text and step numbers, where private details are hidden, and where the picture is cropped and put on a background.

title: Recording
text: Records an area or the whole screen to an MP4, with the microphone, the computer's sound, your camera and the shortcuts you press.

title: Studio
text: The studio turns a screen recording into a finished video: it zooms in where you clicked, cuts out the dull parts, draws a large smooth cursor, puts the video on a background with the camera in a corner, and exports MP4 or GIF.

title: History
text: Every screenshot, recording and GIF in your screenshots and recordings folders, newest first, as a grid of thumbnails.

title: Settings
text: Settings controls capture behaviour, shortcuts, the editor and studio defaults, and storage.

title: Project files
text: A .kadr project keeps an edit, not just its finished picture or video.

title: Command line
text: Run kadr --help to see the command list.

title: Glossary
text: The words this manual and kadr use.

title: Roadmap
text: The goal: as good and as complete as the best dedicated screenshot and screen-recording tools (capture, the picker, the editor, recording, the studio), and clearly better than what the systems ship with.

title: Linux (Hyprland)
text: Install gpu-screen-recorder, ffmpeg, tesseract with English language data, grim and wl-clipboard.

title: macOS and Windows
text: For a source build, build all three programs and keep kadr, kadr-tray and kadr-overlay side by side…

title: Updating
text: With General → Check for updates on in Settings, the tray checks once a day.

title: Commands
text: kadr install-desktop is Linux-only.

title: How to open
text: The capture bar (kadr capture) puts every mode on one bar, so one hotkey is enough.

title: The capture bar
text: The bar shows near the bottom of the screen with eight modes in three groups…

title: Picking an area
text: The screen freezes, and you drag a box over it.

title: Windows, screens and scrolling
text: A window comes by itself, whatever covers it, with rounded corners and a soft shadow on a transparent background.

title: The card after a capture
text: A card with the picture slides in at the corner of the screen.

title: Pinning
text: A pinned picture floats above every window, at its real size, so you can keep a reference in sight while you work.

title: Text recognition
text: kadr text freezes the screen; pick an area, and its text goes to the clipboard.

title: Keys
text: The capture bar, Picking an area, A pinned picture

title: Settings
text: Text recognition's languages are in Settings → Text.

title: Commands
text: kadr capture, kadr shot, kadr open, kadr pin, kadr text

title: How to open
text: From the card after a screenshot: Edit.

title: Tools
text: The tools sit in the top bar, in groups.

title: Colour, size and a shape's options
text: Colour and size stay in the top bar's corner.

title: Background and presets
text: The background button in the top bar opens a sidebar…

title: Crop
text: C (or the crop button in the top bar) opens the crop mode.

title: The canvas and the bottom bar
text: The canvas zooms: Ctrl and the mouse wheel zoom at the pointer, the wheel alone or Space with a drag pans.

title: Keys
text: Ctrl is Cmd on macOS.

title: Settings
text: Open the editor (Settings → Screenshots → After a screenshot): open every new screenshot in the editor.

title: Commands
text: kadr edit, kadr open

title: How to open
text: The hotkey. On macOS and Windows the default is Ctrl+Shift+2; on Linux kadr starts from your Hyprland bindings.

title: The recording bar
text: The bar sits under the area (or above it, or inside it, where there's no room), and the rest of the screen is dimmed.

title: While recording
text: A small bar stays by the area, outside it, so it isn't recorded.

title: The camera bubble
text: Turn on Camera in the recording bar, and a live picture of your camera shows over the area.

title: After recording
text: Without studio mode a card shows in the corner of the screen, with the recording's length.

title: On macOS and Windows
text: Recording there goes through the system's own capture and encoder, with the system's sound and the default microphone.

title: Keys
text: Enter: Record (in the recording bar)

title: Settings
text: How long the card stays and where it shows are in Settings → General (see Capture).

title: Commands
text: kadr record, kadr trim, kadr gif

title: How to open
text: From the card after a recording: Studio.

title: The window
text: The rail at the left has the sections: Zoom, Cursor, Keyboard shortcuts, Audio, Camera, Background, and Cut apart at the bottom.

title: Zooms and cuts
text: Zoom. A studio mode recording comes with zooms already placed on your clicks; for any other recording, add them yourself.

title: Cursor, shortcuts, camera and audio
text: For a studio mode recording: Show the cursor, its Size (0.5× to 3×), Style (Arrow, Light arrow or Dot) and Motion (Natural or Smooth).

title: Background and export
text: Presets at the top: + saves the current look (background, padding, cursor, export), the dropdown picks, renames or deletes one.

title: Platforms
text: Clicks and keys are logged by kadr's Hyprland hook, so on Linux only for now.

title: Screenshots
text: kadr capture opens the bar with every capture mode.

title: Recording

text: kadr edit <image|project.kadr> opens the editor; kadr studio <video|project.kadr> opens the studio, and its render flag exports immediately.

title: 1. Capture
text: An area, a window, the whole screen, every screen: kadr shot all; windows on M/W from the system's list (W: EnumWindows + WindowFromPoint)

title: 2. The card
text: A card after a capture: open, edit, copy, save, delete

title: 3. Editor
text: Arrow: 4 styles, curved too: filled head, open head, both ends, tapered, all of them bend; M/W: drawing checked by golden tests in CI, picking a style only by e2e on Linux

title: 4. Pin on top, history, text recognition
text: Pin on top: size, opacity, move by a pixel with the arrows, let clicks through: M/W: unchecked; letting clicks through is in doubt

title: 5. Platform and behaviour
text: Tray or menu bar icon with quick actions, start at login

title: 6. Recording
text: Record an area, a window or the screen; MP4 (H.264) and GIF: a window is recorded as an area; M/W: the screen is checked in CI, an area isn't

title: 7. Studio
text: Timeline: trim, cuts, dragging pieces around: M/W: the studio hasn't been tried on a real machine; export needs ffmpeg with libplacebo

title: 8. Agent mode, kadr's own (SPEC §11)
text: kadr mcp: capture / windows / record.start / record.marker / record.stop / studio.export / ocr

title: 9. Beyond parity
text: Scrolling capture on macOS and Windows: The systems' own tools lack it; now on all three, M/W pass desktop-e2e (see section 1)
